Qubes OS is built around one brutally honest idea: assume a breach. Instead of trusting your browser, files, passwords, work documents, and sensitive data in one shared environment like Windows, macOS, or a typical Linux install, Qubes separates everything into isolated compartments called qubes, so one mistake doesn't compromise your entire computer. 

In this overview I walk through how Qubes OS actually works. I explain what a qube is (an isolated security compartment implemented as a virtual machine, but integrated into one desktop so apps sit side by side), and why the colored window borders matter, with a personal qube in yellow and a work qube in blue running Firefox at the same time. title: Qubes OS explained: assume you will get hacked
